title: Run real-Git drive-path export tests on Windows without skips
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Two real-Git export regressions are skipped on Windows because their fixtures create colon-bearing filenames. This replaces those worktree fixtures with actual Git blobs, NUL-delimited trees and a commit, so **all five drive-path tests execute on Windows without skips**.

The fixtures assert the exact committed names and never materialize the package inputs. The existing CLI still rejects `C:/outside.txt` and `D:outside.txt` before publishing an archive or leaving temporary output. Nondrive colons retain exact names and binary/CRLF payloads; the accepted archive also passes the actual integrity-check CLI with Git absent from `PATH`. Production exporter code, scientific inputs and the selected frontier are unchanged. This is a two-file tooling contribution, with no new κ.

## Task and overlap

Task `portable-replay`, **scope refined** to the open handoff in [Discussion #4578](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4578) and [#1166](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19118044). [Canonical claim and result: #4675](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4675).

Started from canonical main `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7; the final upstream refresh is unchanged. Contribution commit: `46e2377a9a86f99baf622d80df49ac9a154e7b8f`.

Nearest overlap is [#4579](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4579), head `20188e79a19f236eaea5bb67e5fe50411ea76727`: it repairs a different test module and explicitly leaves these two drive-path fixtures open. This patch applies directly to main and does not require that pending test change. Both touch the exporter documentation; retain their separately dated evidence when integrating.

The final helper refresh covered **447 open PR bodies and 3,605 Discussion records**, with reported complete pagination at 15:34–15:36 UTC on October 22. Targeted module/drive-prefix/colon/mktree searches found the predecessor and this claim, not another repair. Local package-note coverage is sparse (2 of 5,860 tracked notes); arbitrary diffs, closed remote PRs and unpublished work are outside this search.

## Validation

| Local environment | Ordinary Python | Optimized Python |
|---|---|---|
| Windows, CPython 3.12.14, Git 2.47.1.windows.1 | 5 drive-path + 5 topology tests pass, no skips | Same 10 pass, no skips |
| Ubuntu/WSL2, CPython 3.12.3, Git 2.43.0 | All 19 exporter tests pass | All 19 pass |

```sh
python -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export_drive_paths.py' -v
python -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export_drive_paths.py' -v
python -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export_topology.py' -v
python -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export_topology.py' -v
# Linux; the separate Windows test_research_export.py repair is pending in #4579.
python -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export*.py' -v
python -O -W error -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_export*.py' -v
git diff --check
```

Three disposable exporter mutations were each rejected by the repaired real-Git tests under optimized Python on **both** platforms: removing drive-prefix rejection, rejecting every colon, and converting CRLF payload bytes to LF while recomputing a self-consistent receipt. On Windows the removed-guard mutation fails the required diagnostic even though Git later rejects the drive path; on Linux the same mutation incorrectly publishes and is caught. The payload mutation reaches the exact-byte assertion.

Both changed working files match their committed Git blobs. Hosted CI and a full mathematical cold replay are not claimed. The selected metadata baseline stopped at a source omitted by the sparse checkout; no construction verification is inferred. The full Windows exporter suite still needs the separate #4579 repair.

## Credit

Retains Tekalign's #3138 exporter/tests and roger-sato's #3629/#3641 boundary regressions. The Git-object fixture approach follows Mihir Srivastava's #4579 precedent. Prepared for **Mihir Srivastava / mihir-s-05 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

None needed within this bounded fixture repair. Maintainer review can assess it independently of #4579. Archive extraction of arbitrary accepted names, a general Windows filename policy and mathematical verification remain outside scope.
